webster.text: That cannot be corrected or amended; bad beyond correction; as incorrigible error.

more.text: Too depraved to be corrected or reformed; as an incorrigible sinner; an incorrigible drunkard.

example.quote: That incorrigible gentleman, being a child of the revolution, must recollect with gratitude the glorious effects of requisitions.
example.cite: Jonathan Elliot, ed., The Debates in the Several State Conventions on the Adoption of the Federal Constitution, vol. 3, Virginia Convention, June 9, 1788 (2d ed. 1836)
